considered_rates.assessment: AU 2Y 4.835, 5Y 4.867, 10Y 5.202 are 99th+ percentile on both 1y and 5y windows as of 2026-09-09, and housing is the fundamental case to own lower AU yields. That is a real valuation stretch, but AU inflation gauge 82 plus Fed hike to 3.75–4.00% and ECB +25bp make long AU duration an inflation-contaminated expression. It also owns only the AU leg and ignores NZDUSD already at 5y 11.5th percentile. AU observations are eight days stale versus the 2026-09-17 FX fix.

AU 2s10s 36.7bp is only 28th percentile 1y / 32nd 5y — not a valuation extreme. US 2s10s 27bp and CA 2s10s 57bp are 1y extremes (pctile_1y 1.39 and 0.79) but 5y percentiles are 56th and 66th, so the flatness is a one-year window artifact, not a five-year mispricing. Curve does not own the AUDNZD peer dislocation.

The economically matched RV for this thesis is AU-NZ 2Y/5Y/10Y; those series are unavailable (RBNZ B2 HTTP 403) and must stay null. AU-US 2Y +40.5bp is 5y 89th percentile (z_5y +1.43) — a milder stretch than AUDNZD z_5y +2.96 and still mixed with a hiking Fed. CA-US 5Y −122bp is a 1y 0.20th percentile extreme, but CA core near 2%, CA labor 38 vs US labor 75, and a hotter US inflation gauge mean cheap Canadian yields versus Treasuries are at least partly fundamental; fading that spread would be statistical mean reversion without a closing mechanism. CA-AU 2Y −167.5bp (5y 8.6th percentile) says AU already pays a large yield premium, which argues against expressing the housing view by shorting AUDCAD through 167bp of 2Y carry.

considered_spot.assessment: The discrepancy lives in the AUD versus NZD peer cross: 5y percentile 99.96, z_5y +2.96, with the USD legs already skewed the same way (AUDUSD 5y 83.5th, NZDUSD 5y 11.5th). Housing is the AU-side closer and the India FTA is the NZ-side closer. Spot owns both legs without fabricating NZ yields.

thesis: Valuation anchor is the five-year AUDNZD distribution and the USD-leg split (rich AUDUSD, cheap NZDUSD), not a post-drop dip-buy.
AU and NZ inflation gauges are similar, so the cross extreme is not an inflation-gap revaluation; it is a peer FX premium that now collides with AU housing transmission and a NZ export-deal impulse.

Comparable-country normalization prefers AUDNZD over AUDCAD: CAD has a separate energy/ToT channel (BoC energy pass-through versus a Saudi supply workaround that eased the oil tail), which muddies the relative-value identity.

trade.structure: outright spot FX; short AUD / long NZD
trade.thesis: The valuation anchor is peer-normalized spot history, not the fact that anything sold off: AUDNZD is at the 99.96th five-year percentile (z_5y +2.96) with AUDUSD already rich (5y 83.5th) and NZDUSD already cheap (5y 11.5th). Comparable-country inflation gauges are similar (AU 82 vs NZ 80), so that extreme AUD premium is not a PPP-like inflation gap. The closing mechanism is a change, not a level: NSW stamp-duty receipts −24% YoY, volumes −18%, and Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% below peak show the RBA tightening channel biting, while NZ’s India FTA (tariffs cut on ~95% of NZ exports to India) is a positive NZ export/ToT impulse. Convergence should start now because the cross is still priced as if AU can keep delivering the yield/FX premium after that housing hole is visible.
why_now: AUDNZD is already at the top of the five-year sample, so entry is statistically stretched after the discrepancy is identified, not instead of it.

AU housing is the new transmission: stamp-duty and transaction collapse is the tightening channel showing up in real activity/fiscal receipts, which is the mechanism that should compress the AUD premium versus NZD.
NZ parliament passing the India trade agreement is independent NZ-side fundamental news that does not belong with a record-rich AUDNZD.
AU outright yields are also historically high, but AU inflation 82 and a live global hike wave make long AU duration a dirtier expression of the same housing story.

what_changes_my_mind: An official NZ yield print that shows a large AU rate premium consistent with z_5y +2.96 in spot.
AU housing stabilization (volumes, prices, or stamp-duty receipts) while NZ labor/activity stay weak.
AU inflation re-accelerating versus NZ, which would make the AUD premium fundamental rather than stretched.
A live executable AUDNZD market that is already materially below the ECB 1.2388 reference, so the historical extreme is an artifact of the fixing.
why_now: Housing evidence is the change that should start compressing the AUD premium while the level of the cross is still at a five-year high.
The India FTA is dated 2026-09-16 and is not already amortized into a 5y-max AUDNZD.
Waiting for NZ official yields would be cleaner, but refusing the matched rates RV is not permission to sit on a 99.96th-percentile cross with a visible AU housing closer.
